We have a unique part\-time opportunity to provide executive leadership for a California\-based client, a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting sustainable and reliable urban water supplies. This position is currently structured as part\-time; however, full\-time opportunities may be available based on the candidate's skills, experience and business needs.



In this role, the individual will serve as Executive Director, leading the client organization in achieving its mission to provide a unified voice for urban water solutions that support thriving communities and a healthy environment. **Job ID** REQ20180601 **Category** Development and Fundraising
  
The University of Southern California (USC), founded in 1880, is a world\-class research university located in the heart of Los Angeles and the city’s largest private employer. As a USC employee, you will become part of the “Trojan Family”—the faculty, students, and staff who make the university an exceptional place to work.


USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences is committed to the creation, preservation, and communication of knowledge, a lifelong passion for learning, and the betterment of society. Realizing this mission requires a culture in which students, faculty, and staff can thrive—one grounded in respect, collaboration, opportunity, and a shared commitment to excellence.


The Director of Development will contribute to this mission by building meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, and friends and securing philanthropic support for the College’s highest priorities. In addition to strong fundraising expertise, the successful candidate will be a collaborative colleague who strengthens relationships, understands their impact on others, and contributes positively to the success of the advancement team and the broader Dornsife community.


**Job Summary**


USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial, and highly motivated **Director of Development** to manage and grow a portfolio of high\-capacity gift prospects and donors, with a primary focus on Hong Kong and a complementary portfolio in Southern California. This is a frontline fundraising role for a seasoned development professional who is energized by building relationships, identifying opportunity, and translating the intellectual and academic strengths of Dornsife into compelling philanthropic investments.


The Director of Development will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors capable of making **gifts of up to $5 million** and will be responsible for driving the full major\-gift cycle—from prospect identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, gift negotiation, and stewardship. The successful candidate will be an independent self\-starter who is comfortable creating a strategy where one does not yet exist, developing trusted relationships with individuals and families, and navigating complex philanthropic interests to connect donors with opportunities across Dornsife’s humanities, social sciences, and life and physical sciences.


Working closely with academic leaders, faculty, University Advancement colleagues, and other development partners, the Director will develop and execute individualized engagement strategies designed to deepen donor affinity, increase philanthropic investment, and secure support for Dornsife’s highest priorities. The role requires exceptional judgment, initiative, cultural fluency, discretion, and the ability to operate effectively across geographies, time zones, and levels of university leadership.


This is an opportunity for a proven major\-gift fundraiser to have meaningful ownership of a significant portfolio and to play a visible role in expanding Dornsife’s philanthropic reach internationally and in Southern California.


**Key Responsibilities**


**Build and manage a major\-gift portfolio.** Manage a portfolio of approximately 75 high\-potential prospects and donors, with a particular emphasis on individuals and families based in Hong Kong and Southern California. Develop and continually refine sophisticated relationship strategies that reflect each donor’s interests, capacity, connections, and philanthropic objectives.


**Identify and qualify new prospects.** Identify, research, qualify, and engage prospective donors with the capacity and inclination to make significant investments in USC Dornsife. Develop networks and referral sources that expand the College’s pipeline, particularly within international markets. This work will be supported by research teams in University Advancement and Dornsife Advancement.


**Drive the complete major\-gift process.** Personally lead prospects through discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, taking ownership of outcomes and maintaining momentum across a complex and often lengthy fundraising cycle.


**Structure Transformative gifts.** Partner with donors, their advisors, and university colleagues to structure significant and complex gifts that align donor intent with Dornsife priorities and university policies.


**Develop compelling philanthropic opportunities.** Work with academic and university leaders to translate Dornsife’s priorities into clear, persuasive, donor\-centered opportunities. Develop customized proposals, briefing materials, talking points, and other communications that articulate the impact and significance of philanthropic investment.


**Cultivate relationships with senior\-level donors and advisors.** Establish and sustain relationships characterized by trust, credibility, and discretion. **Represent USC Dornsife in Hong Kong and Southern California.** Travel regularly to meet with prospects and donors, participate in cultivation and stewardship activities, attend events, and build a strong network of relationships that advances Dornsife’s visibility and fundraising objectives.


**Partner across the university.** Collaborate closely with academic leadership, faculty, University Advancement colleagues, major and principal gifts teams, corporate and foundation relations, planned giving, prospect management, and other partners to develop coordinated and effective fundraising strategies. **About VetPowered LLC**
========================


VetPowered was founded in 2009 to support Workshops for Warriors (wfw.org), an accredited 501(c)(3\) nonprofit school that trains, certifies, and places veterans and transitioning service members into dignified lifelong careers in advanced manufacturing to Rebuild America’s Manufacturing Force…One Veteran at a Time. Workshops for Warriors has trained and certified 1,776 veterans and transitioning service members, awarded nearly 23,000 industry credentials, and placed graduates at 522 companies across 49 states. The average starting wage for a WFW graduate is $63,500\.


Our goal is to train veterans for dignified lifelong careers and make America the world’s manufacturing superpower again.


That is the story almost nobody has heard. This role exists to change that, and to turn the telling of it into purchase orders, partnerships, and product revenue. This will allow us to create scholarships, provide housing, and build brighter futures for the men and women who honorably served our nation.

**Position Overview**
=====================


VetPowered, LLC is seeking a dynamic and highly organized candidate for the position of Personal Aide to the Chief Executive Officer. In this vital role, you will serve as primary support for a busy CEO, helping ensure smooth daily operations and efficient management of personal and administrative tasks.


The CEO has many time\-sensitive commitments, both professionally and personally, and is continually creating and pursuing growth opportunities for multi\-million\-dollar organizations. Your proactive approach, exceptional organizational skills, and attention to detail will help create an efficient and productive working environment.


Most importantly, this position requires patience, a pleasant demeanor, the ability to listen well, a sense of urgency, and the ability to follow directions. Reliability is a must.


This is a full personal and administrative support position and is not appropriate for candidates who wish to perform only in\-office administrative duties. Candidates with prior experience assisting very busy, Type A individuals are encouraged to apply. The information below is intended to provide transparent expectations for this key support role.

**Purpose of the Position**
===========================


At VetPowered, LLC, the Personal Aide exists so that the Chief Executive Officer can spend his time on the work that only he can do. The role removes recurring, time\-consuming, and personal tasks that would otherwise consume hours of every day or be improperly assigned to senior officers of the organization.


This position performs work that would not be asked of the Chief Operating Officer, Chief of Staff, or Executive Aide. That distinction defines the role.


The Personal Aide is accountable for the readiness and order of the Chief Executive Officer’s working environment, the continuity of his personal and household affairs, and the complete execution of any assigned task that is legal, ethical, safe, and consistent with the mission.


This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working behind the scenes to keep things organized. The ideal candidate will anticipate the CEO’s needs, maintain workspace readiness, and take pride in making his day easier. This hands\-on role requires discretion, flexibility, and the ability to thrive in a fast\-paced environment where no two days are the same.

**Duties, Responsibilities \& Expectations**
============================================

**Workspace Readiness**
-----------------------


The office of the Chief Executive Officer and all adjoining workspaces are the responsibility of this position.

* Ensure the office, desk, work surfaces, and adjoining workspaces are clean, cleared, vacuumed, and organized before the Chief Executive Officer arrives each morning.
* Maintain order in the space throughout the day and reset it at the close of business.
* No outside cleaning contractor, building custodial staff, or other personnel may clean or organize the personal space of the Chief Executive Officer. This work is performed by the Personal Aide.
* Maintain supplies, materials, and equipment so that nothing is missing when it is needed.

**Meal Service and Hospitality**
--------------------------------


Meals with senior staff and guests are a working instrument of leadership. This position ensures those meals happen properly without consuming the time of the Chief Executive Officer or other officers of the organization.

* Order, obtain, prepare, plate, and serve breakfast, lunch, dinner, refreshments, and snacks for the Chief Executive Officer and for guests or staff members he designates.
* Set the table and surrounding space in advance so that the Chief Executive Officer and his guests sit down to a complete and ready setting.
* Ensure meals are fresh, wholesome, and nutritious, while accounting for the dietary requirements of guests.
* Clear, clean, and reset the space at the conclusion of the meal without interrupting work in progress.
* Provide hospitality support for visitors, tours, and guests hosted by the Chief Executive Officer.

\*\*\*TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION CANDIDATES MUST BE PERMANENT IN THE TITLE OF ADMINISTRATIVE PUBLIC INFORMATION SPECIALIST. ALL OTHER CANDIDATES WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED\*\*\*.
  

  

The Commission on Human Rights (the “Commission”) is the City agency charged with enforcing the New York City Human Rights Law (“City Human Rights Law”), one of the most expansive civil rights laws in the nation, prohibiting discrimination in housing, employment, and public accommodations. The Commission investigates, litigates, and adjudicates claims of discrimination brought by the public. Where the Commission finds unlawful discrimination, harassment, and retaliation have occurred, it obtains compensation to victims, orders companies to take corrective action, and can assess civil penalties. The Commission also engages in training and education to ensure New Yorkers understand their rights and responsibilities under City Law.
  

  

The Director of Communications reports to the Deputy Commissioner of External Affairs and works to develop and implement the communications and public relations strategy for the agency. The Director of Communications leads a team of communications professionals to advance the agency’s mission and execute strategies that advance awareness of the NYCHRL, the CCHR activities, and human rights issues impacting New Yorkers. The position collaborates with agency stakeholders, media, press, bloggers, advocates, community groups, elected officials and the general public.

* Develop communications and marketing strategies to advance Commission goals.
* Manage the agency’s communication budget.

* Identify new campaigns to educate New Yorkers about rights and obligations under the Human Rights Law (HRL).
* Develop and build positive relationships with media, elected officials, agency stakeholders and the community.
* Convene focus groups and utilize other research techniques, to inform the development and evaluate the impact of campaign strategies.
* Develop and disseminate multi\-lingual materials to educate New Yorkers about their rights and obligations under the HRL.
* Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with journalists, including ethnic media editors and other contacts as appropriate in print and broadcast media.
* Act as an agency spokesperson and serve as a key contact for media, elected officials, agency stakeholders and the community.

* Supervise staff in the Communications Team and support professional development through assignments and training opportunities.

**About Us**



Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.  


It is Kardigan's mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan's co\-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020\.

We have a cutting\-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late\-stage candidates, and an industry\-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

The Illinois Valley Watershed Council (IVWC) is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit Oregon Plan watershed council serving the Illinois Valley — one of Oregon’s most geographically remote and economically distressed communities, and home to some of the most ecologically significant salmon habitat remaining in the Pacific Northwest. Shape the Next Chapter of a Community Landmark

The Newport Opera House Association (NOHA) is seeking an energetic, collaborative Executive Director to bring people together through performances, theatre, education, and community events. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will lead programming, fundraising, operations, marketing and public relations, partnerships, and the stewardship of NOHA's resources and reputation. The right candidate will be equally comfortable building relationships with the NOHA community, local community leaders, donors and Town officials, developing annual season activities, managing financial and operational budgets, promoting events, and solving the unexpected challenges that come with live performance.

· Create an affordable, engaging annual season of performances, community theatre, educational programs, and special events.

· Produce at least two community\-based theatrical productions each year and expand opportunities for children and families.

· Grow individual and corporate memberships, sponsorships, grants, major gifts, and other mission\-aligned revenue.

· Build strong relationships with audiences, donors, artists, volunteers, businesses, schools, community organizations, the media, and municipal partners.

· Manage event production, contracts, ticketing, marketing, staffing, technical coordination, and front\-of\-house operations.

· Develop and manage the annual budget, monitor financial performance, strengthen internal controls, and provide clear reports to the Board.

· Fundraising Track Record \- A record of success in fundraising, grant writing, memberships, sponsorships, or donor engagement.

· Fiscal Acumen \- Experience creating and managing budgets and interpreting financial reports.

· Strong event or project\-management skills, with the ability to coordinate many people, details, and deadlines.

· Communication Skills \- Excellent writing, public\-speaking, relationship\-building, and problem\-solving skills.

· Strong Community Collaboration \- Comfort working with a volunteer Board and collaborating across a close\-knit community.

Especially Valuable Qualifications

· Experience producing theatre, performing\-arts events, or educational programs.

· Experience in a grassroots, rural, start\-up, or small\-community organization.

· Knowledge of Newport and the Lake Sunapee Region.

· A degree in arts administration, nonprofit management, business, public administration, theatre, or a related field—or equivalent professional experience.

· Experience with QuickBooks, Arts People or similar ticketing/CRM systems, digital marketing, and grant management.

This role offers the chance to strengthen a treasured community institution, champion local creativity, introduce audiences to new experiences, and build sustainable support for the arts. New Bedford Research \& Robotics

**Director of Operations**


New Bedford, MA \| Full time, onsite \| $85,000 to $110,000

**Opportunity**
===============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics (NBRR) is a nonprofit innovation center where advanced technology and creative work happen on a downtown campus. We help entrepreneurs advance new products, run education and workforce programs, and support research. Founders, students, artists, and engineers work in the same rooms and use the same machines.


On any given day you might see a teenager learning industrial robotics, a marine robotics startup testing a vehicle, an artist in residence making a ceramic bowl with a robot, and an engineer refining a new process. Our campus comprises four buildings on “innovation alley” in New Bedford, and will expand from 15,000 to 33,000 square feet this year when we expand our headquarters.


Our home is a legacy site, the old Glaser Glass building, where for many decades people cut and fit glass for this city's cars, houses, and boats. The tools have changed. What happens inside has not: people learning a trade, testing an idea, and finding out whether it works.


This new role is coming at a time of growth at NBRR. We are looking for a person who understands NBRR’s mission and vision, and has the experience and operational leadership skills to scale, balance, and innovate.

**About NBRR**
==============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics’s programs are designed to stand on their own and to make each other better where they overlap:

* Industry R\&D: aerospace, manufacturing, marine tech, architecture and construction, e\-mobility
* Startups in residence: marine robotics, advanced manufacturing, medical, fashion, data, construction
* Research: AI, robotics, design, new materials
* Community: paid internships, a lecture series, artist and designer residencies
* Education and workforce development: marine robotics, industrial robotics, STEAM


NBRR’s staff of engineers, designers, and educators work across all of it, which is how ideas move between a classroom, a startup, and a manufacturer’s research problem.


Today we have seven full\-time staff, two fractional discipline leaders, 20 to 30 interns a year, and a startup membership on track to reach 25 companies in 2027, alongside partner organizations, universities, and schools. Late fall we will open 18,000 square feet of newly fitted out space.

**The Role**
============


This new position will be the senior operating role at NBRR \- focused on orchestrating and systematizing the ecosystem of programs and people that bring our mission to life. Our campus and technology set the stage for NBRR’s team, startups, interns, research partnerships, and community impact. We’re in pursuit of an experienced and vision\-driven person who can maintain balance and contribute to growth across our programs.

**How This Works With the CEO**
===============================


You would report to Mark Parsons, our Founder and CEO. Here is how we see the roles:

* The CEO owns vision and strategy, fundraising, major external relationships, and the board.
* You would own execution and the daily running of the organization: operations, administration, and facilities.
* You would make routine operational, vendor, and personnel decisions within the approved budget.
* You and the CEO will keep a standing cadence to align on priorities, risks, staffing, and what is coming next.
* You would prepare for and present to the Board of Directors at its quarterly meetings.

**Your Areas of Responsibility**
================================

**People and administration**
-----------------------------

* Turn organizational priorities into plans with owners, timelines, and follow\-through.
* Build and manage the operating team, including a site manager, as we grow.
* With the CEO, hold a culture built on clear communication, accountability, collaboration, and honest feedback.
* Support our department leaders in delivering their programs.
* Serve as first line contact to outside HR, finance, IT, and other providers.
* Make sure the way we recruit interns, hire staff, and fill programs reaches the whole community.
* Keep HR practice current with our HR partner: policies, documentation, onboarding, and performance conversations.

**Systems**
-----------

* Build the annual operating calendar, the workflows, and the accountability systems that make follow\-through visible.
* Evolve and maintain the policies and standard operating procedures a growing organization needs, sized to the organization we actually are.
* Own contracts, insurance, risk management, records, and compliance.
* Name capacity problems early and bring the staffing, vendor, or process answer.

**Community and members**
-------------------------

* Own what it feels like to be here. The member experience is the systems plus everything else: how fast someone gets an answer or whether a new member knows five people by their second week.
* Make sure our 20 to 30 interns a year continue to have a home that is well\-run so they can have a genuinely transformative experience here. They contribute to research and operations, and they are part of the work rather than adjacent to it.
* Support relationship building with community members and partner organizations, coordinating with the CEO and our organizational leaders.

**Campus**
----------

* Run the four\-building, 33,000 square foot campus, located next to the downtown cultural district, a $2B deep water port and the new rail station for the train to Boston.
* Set the facility practices that keep the place efficient, safe, secure, clean, well used, and earning revenue.
* Oversee IT, capital equipment, and building systems, along with the service agreements behind them.

**What Success Looks Like in the First Year**
=============================================

* The expansion into NBRR’s new headquarters is successful. The new space opens and settles, the campus absorbs growth

**About VetPowered LLC**
========================


VetPowered was founded in 2009 to support Workshops for Warriors (wfw.org), an accredited 501(c)(3\) nonprofit school that trains, certifies, and places veterans and transitioning service members into dignified lifelong careers in advanced manufacturing to Rebuild America’s Manufacturing Force…One Veteran at a Time. Workshops for Warriors has trained and certified 1,776 veterans and transitioning service members, awarded nearly 23,000 industry credentials, and placed graduates at 522 companies across 49 states. The average starting wage for a WFW graduate is $63,500\.


Our goal is to train veterans for dignified lifelong careers and make America the world’s manufacturing superpower again.


That is the story almost nobody has heard. This role exists to change that, and to turn the telling of it into purchase orders, partnerships, and product revenue. This will allow us to create scholarships, provide housing, and build brighter futures for the men and women who honorably served our nation.

**Position Overview**
=====================


VetPowered, LLC is seeking a dynamic and highly organized candidate for the position of Personal Aide to the Chief Executive Officer. In this vital role, you will serve as primary support for a busy CEO, helping ensure smooth daily operations and efficient management of personal and administrative tasks.


The CEO has many time\-sensitive commitments, both professionally and personally, and is continually creating and pursuing growth opportunities for multi\-million\-dollar organizations. Your proactive approach, exceptional organizational skills, and attention to detail will help create an efficient and productive working environment.


Most importantly, this position requires patience, a pleasant demeanor, the ability to listen well, a sense of urgency, and the ability to follow directions. Reliability is a must.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working behind the scenes to keep things organized. This hands\-on role requires discretion, flexibility, and the ability to thrive in a fast\-paced environment where no two days are the same.
